title: CallSpec JSON-Lite: compact parameter definition + graceful validation and compatibility fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Define a compact, deterministic JSON schema subset (CallSpec JSON-Lite) for function/tool parameter declarations used by the Core API. Provide clear runtime validation ordering, classified error messages, and a compatibility layer with deterministic coercion rules to handle legacy clients and imperfect LLM outputs. The goal is to reduce developer confusion, minimize fatal failures in production, and enable safe rollouts where strictness can be increased over time.

Motivation / background:
- Current validation landscape is fragmented: full JSON Schema is powerful but heavyweight; multiple runtime adaptations have led to inconsistent error messages and recovery strategies across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- LLM outputs and third-party tools sometimes emit types in subtly wrong formats (e.g., numeric-as-string, snake_case param names). We should accept reasonable variants by default and surface telemetry and opt-in strict modes for customers who want exact enforcement.

Proposal (high level):
1) CallSpec JSON-Lite format: a deterministic, small subset of JSON Schema tailored to function/tool parameter spec. Key supported fields: type, enum, required, default, description, pattern (limited), items.type (primitive arrays only), min/max for numeric, minLength/maxLength for strings, deprecated (boolean) and renamed_to (string) for compatibility mapping. All fields and examples in the spec are intentionally limited to keep runtime simple.

2) Validation pipeline (deterministic order):
  - Parse incoming call metadata (content-type checks)
  - Key normalization pass (snake_case <-> camelCase mapping)
  - Coercion pass (per-field rules like string->number when numeric pattern, comma-separated string->array for items.type, bool coercion from 'true'/'false' strings)
  - Structural validation (presence of required keys; type checks against CallSpec JSON-Lite types)
  - Semantic validators (range checks, enum membership, regex pattern match)
  - Post-validation hooks (deprecated warnings, rename migration via renamed_to)
  - Final canonicalization (produce normalized param map sent to runtime)

3) Error classification and codes: each validation error produced by runtime will include a stable error code, HTTP mapping (4xx/5xx), and a "severity" flag: recoverable | fatal | warned. Examples (template):
  - ERR_PARAM_MISSING (fatal): "Required parameter '{name}' is missing."
  - ERR_INVALID_TYPE (recoverable): "Parameter '{name}' expected {expected} but received {received}; attempted coercion to {expected} succeeded/failed."
  - ERR_ENUM_MISMATCH (recoverable): "Parameter '{name}' has value '{value}' which is not one of allowed {allowed_values}."
  - ERR_EXTRA_PARAM (warned): "Parameter '{name}' is not declared in CallSpec and will be ignored."
  - ERR_DEPRECATION (warned): "Parameter '{old}' is deprecated; use '{new}' instead. Will be automatically mapped for now."

4) Compatibility layer rules (defaults):
  - Key normalization: support camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case mapping by default. If both fooBar and foo_bar present, return ERR_INVALID_CONFLICT (fatal).
  - Numeric coercion: accept numeric strings if they parse unambiguously (leading/trailing whitespace trimmed). If parsing fails, return ERR_INVALID_TYPE.
  - Boolean coercion: accept 'true'/'false' (case-insensitive), 1/0.
  - Array coercion: accept comma-separated strings for primitive arrays when items.type is primitive. Empty string -> empty array only if minItems allows.
  - Date/time: accept ISO-8601 strings for date/datetime types; do NOT implicitly parse ambiguous forms.

5) Strict mode vs permissive mode:
  - Default (per-tenant) is permissive with telemetry and warned errors.
  - Customers can opt-in to strict mode (enforced via tenant config or request-level header) where many recoverable errors become fatal and coercion is disabled.

6) Telemetry and metrics (required):
  - Emit validation.events with tags: error_code, severity, call_spec_id, model_family, tenant_id, route_id.
  - Counters for each error_code and per-route distribution.
  - Histogram for validation.latency.

7) Rollout plan and canarying:
  - Implement new validator behind a feature flag.
  - Internal canary: route 1% of internal traffic with permissive mode; surface logs in QA workspace.
  - External canary: opt-in tenant set (support + beta customers) with permissive mode.
  - Ramp rules: ramp to 25%/50%/100% over 2 weeks after no fatal regression signals.

8) Backwards compatibility and migration guidance for integrators:
  - Provide a validation preview API that returns errors/warnings on sample calls without executing tool.
  - Automatic rename mapping using renamed_to with warn-only by default.
  - Offer a CLI lint tool that checks CallSpec docs and local test vectors.

Acceptance criteria (tests & behavior):
- Unit tests for each coercion rule and error code (examples included below).
- E2E integration test that feeds an LLM-like noisy payload and verifies normalized canonicalization.
- Telemetry emitted for every validation event and end-to-end dashboards in Console.
- Migration docs and lint CLI published to developers.redwood.com/docs/callspec.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We intentionally avoid supporting full JSON Schema to keep runtime simple and deterministic. Complex schema constructs (oneOf, anyOf, patternProperties) are out of scope.
- Coercion is powerful but can hide data quality issues; hence default to permissive + telemetry and provide strict opt-in.
- Performance: validation happens on the request path. Implement in C++/Rust core runtime extension for Dedicated and Private, with a fallback managed layer for hosted early rollout. Keep pathless allocations minimal and reuse compiled CallSpec runtime artifacts.

Example CallSpec JSON-Lite (compact):
{ "call_spec_id": "user.create_v2", "params": { "email": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^\\S+@\\S+\\.\\S+$", "required": true}, "age": {"type": "integer", "min": 0, "default": 18}, "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}, "is_admin": {"type": "boolean", "deprecated": true, "renamed_to": "roles"} } }

Example runtime errors returned (JSON payload shape):
- fatal error example:
  {"error_code":"ERR_PARAM_MISSING","message":"Required parameter 'email' is missing.","severity":"fatal"}
- recoverable w/ coercion example:
  {"error_code":"ERR_INVALID_TYPE","message":"Parameter 'age' expected integer but received string '23'; coercion succeeded.","severity":"recoverable","normalized_value":23}
- warned extra param example:
  {"error_code":"ERR_EXTRA_PARAM","message":"Parameter 'legacyFlag' is not in CallSpec and will be ignored.","severity":"warned"}

- Add language SDK helpers that accept permissive values and emit client-side lint warnings.
- Add runtime policy to auto-promote warned mapping to fatal after a configured grace period per-tenant.
